title: How long is it?
goal: I can compare and measure lengths. I can use a ruler, also when the object does not start at 0.

learn.intro: To measure, use equal units with no gaps. A cube, a clip and a centimetre (cm) are units. On a ruler, count the spaces, not the marks.

example.problem: A crayon lies on a ruler. It starts at the 4 cm mark and ends at the 11 cm mark. How long is the crayon?
steps: Find where the crayon starts: the 4 mark. It does not start at 0.
Find where it ends: the 11 mark.
Count the spaces from 4 to 11. Hop once for each space: 7 hops.

howto.title: How to measure with a ruler
steps: Find the mark where the object starts.
Find the mark where it ends.
Count the spaces, or subtract: end mark - start mark.

try.text: A marker lies on the ruler. How long is the marker? {b} cm
try.explanation: The marker starts at 2 and ends at 8. Subtract: 8 - 2 = 6. Check by counting the spaces from 2 to 8: 6 hops.

items.text: Look at the 3 strips of cubes.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Strip B is {b} cubes longer than strip A.

items.explanation: Count the cubes: A has 5, B has 8, C has 3. B is longest and C is shortest. 8 - 5 = 3, so B is 3 cubes longer than A.

items.text: A tape is 13 cubes long. A strip is 8 cubes long. Fill in the blank. The tape is {b} cubes longer.
items.explanation: "How many longer" asks for the gap. 13 - 8 = 5. Check: 8 + 5 = 13.
Find the smallest number first (6), then 9, 12 and 14. The shortest length has the fewest cubes.

items.text: A rope is 15 cubes long. Ali cuts off 6 cubes. How long is the piece that is left? {b} cubes
items.explanation: Cutting off takes away. 15 - 6 = 9. Check: 9 + 6 = 15.

items.text: Mei and Ben measure a pencil with cubes. Look at the pencil and the 2 rows.

parts.label: b
parts.text: What is wrong in the other row?   {circ:a gap|cubes overlap}

items.explanation: Ben's 7 cubes touch each other and fit the pencil exactly. Mei's cubes have a gap in the middle, so her row runs past the end of the pencil. Cubes must be end to end with no gaps.

items.text: A tape is 8 cubes long. A strip is 5 cubes longer than the tape. How long is the strip? {b} cubes
items.explanation: "Longer than" means add. 8 + 5 = 13. Check: 13 - 8 = 5.

items.text: Look at the ruler. How long is the crayon? {b} cm
items.explanation: The crayon starts at the 0 mark and ends at the 7 mark. It is 7 cm long.

items.text: Look at the ruler. How long is the pencil? {b} cm
items.explanation: The pencil starts at 4, not at 0. Count the spaces from 4 to 9: 5 spaces. Or subtract: 9 - 4 = 5.

items.text: Look at the ruler. How long is the ribbon? {b} cm
items.explanation: Start at the 3 mark and end at the 12 mark. 12 - 3 = 9. Check: count 9 spaces.

items.text: A leaf lies between the 9 cm and 15 cm marks of a ruler. Write its length. {b} cm
items.explanation: Subtract the start from the end: 15 - 9 = 6. Check: from 9, hop 6 spaces to reach 15.

items.text: Look at the ruler.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The red tape is {b} cm long.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The blue tape is {b} cm long.

items.explanation: Red goes from 1 to 8: 8 - 1 = 7 cm. Blue goes from 3 to 9: 9 - 3 = 6 cm. 7 is more than 6, so the red tape is longer.

items.text: A straw is 6 cm long. Its start is at the 4 cm mark of a ruler. Where is its end? The {b} cm mark
items.explanation: Start at 4 and add the length: 4 + 6 = 10. The straw ends at the 10 cm mark.

items.text: 1 stick is as long as 5 cubes. Fill in the blanks.

parts.label: a
parts.text: 3 sticks are as long as {b} cubes.

parts.label: b
parts.text: 20 cubes are as long as {b} sticks.

parts.label: c
parts.text: 2 sticks and 3 cubes are as long as {b} cubes.

items.explanation: (a) 3 sticks are 5 + 5 + 5 = 15 cubes. (b) 20 cubes make 4 groups of 5, so 4 sticks. (c) 2 sticks are 10 cubes, and 3 more cubes make 13.

items.text: A table is 6 pencils long. The same table is 9 rubbers long. Which is longer, a pencil or a rubber?   {circ:a pencil|a rubber}
items.explanation: The table is the same. The table needs fewer pencils, so each pencil is longer. A pencil is longer than a rubber. More pieces does not mean a longer piece.

items.text: A ribbon is 24 cubes long. Ravi cuts it into 4 pieces of equal length.
items.hint: Draw the ribbon as one bar. Mark the 4 pieces.
items.explanation: 4 equal pieces: 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24, so each piece is 6 cubes. Cut between the pieces: 3 cuts make 4 pieces. The last piece needs no cut.

items.text: A clip is the same length as 2 cubes. A pen is 5 clips long. A bag is 2 pens long.
items.explanation: The pen is 5 clips, and each clip is 2 cubes: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10 cubes. The bag is 2 pens: 10 + 10 = 20 cubes.

items.text: A pencil starts at mark 3 of a ruler. It ends at mark 10. A crayon is 2 cm longer. It starts at mark 2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The crayon ends at the {b} cm mark.

items.hint: Find the pencil's length first. Then the crayon's.
items.explanation: The pencil is 10 - 3 = 7 cm long. The crayon is 2 cm longer, so it is 9 cm long. It starts at 2, so it ends at 2 + 9 = 11. Check: 11 - 2 = 9.

items.text: A fence has 6 posts in a row. Each gap between 2 posts is 3 cubes wide. Ignore how wide a post is.

parts.label: b
parts.text: From the first post to the last post is {b} cubes.

parts.label: c
parts.text: A fence with 10 posts has {b} gaps.

items.hint: Count the gaps, not the posts. How many gaps for 2 posts?
items.explanation: (a) Posts and gaps alternate. The first post has no gap before it, so 6 posts have 5 gaps. (b) 5 gaps of 3 cubes: 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 15. (c) 10 posts have 10 - 1 = 9 gaps. There is always 1 gap fewer than posts.

items.text: 1 rod is as long as 4 cubes. Ali's rope is 3 rods and 2 cubes long. Mei's rope is 14 cubes long.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Which rope is longer?   {circ:Ali's|Mei's|They are the same}

items.hint: Change the rods into cubes first.
items.explanation: Ali's rope: 3 rods are 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 cubes, and 2 more cubes make 14. Mei's rope is also 14 cubes. The ropes are the same length.

items.text: A rope is 14 cubes long. Ben cuts it into pieces of 3 cubes or 4 cubes. Nothing is left over. How many pieces of each?

rows: {b} pieces of 4 cubes and {b} pieces of 3 cubes.

items.hint: Try 1 piece of 4 cubes. What is left?
items.explanation: One 4-cube piece leaves 10 cubes, and 3-cube pieces cannot fill 10. Two 4-cube pieces leave 6 cubes, and 3 + 3 = 6. So 4 + 4 + 3 + 3 = 14. Three 4-cube pieces leave 2 cubes, which a 3-cube piece cannot fill.

items.text: A stick lies from 5 cm to 13 cm. How long is it? {b} cm
items.explanation: The stick starts at 5 and ends at 13. 13 - 5 = 8.

items.text: Ravi's string is 14 cubes. Lily's is 9. Ravi's is {b} cubes longer.
1 bar is as long as 3 cubes. 5 bars are as long as {b} cubes.
Tape A is 8 cubes. B is 3 cubes longer than A. C is 2 cubes shorter than A.
items.explanation: B is 8 + 3 = 11 cubes. C is 8 - 2 = 6 cubes. A is 8 cubes. 11 is the greatest, so B is longest.
